summary:
[  edit  ]
The Clock  CHOP  generates channels that reflect the time of year, month, week, day, hour, minute, second and millisecond. It also has a moon cycle channel. It provides the date as separate channels and in different units. It presents the time in two ways:
It generates  0-1 ramps  that reflect the time of year, month, week, day, hour, minute, second and millisecond.
It generates  integers that reflects the day-of month  etc. In this form the year channel is 4 for 2004, etc.
It generates a countdown to a specific date.
There are sunrise/sunset features, and you can override the day-of-year by inputting 1-6 channels into the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Output
parameters.name: output
parameters.description: ⊞  - Fractions or Units affects the channel data that is output from the Clock  CHOP . Fraction gives convenient 0-1 ramps and Units give integers, like 0-23 for the hours of a day. For example, use Fractions and the day, hour and minute channels to drive a wall clock.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.name: units
parameters.description: Generates  integers that reflect the day-of month  etc. In this form the year channel is 4 for 2004, etc.

parameters.label: Fractions
parameters.name: fractions
parameters.description: Generates  0-1 ramps  that reflect the time of year, month, week, day, hour, minute, second and millisecond.

parameters.label: Countdown
parameters.name: countdown
parameters.description: Runs in a  Countdown  mode. The first input should contain channels name year, month, day, hour, min, sec and msec. Any missing values are assumed to be midnight January 1st of specified year. The second input is entirely optional, missing values are taken from current time. For year values, 25 means 2025, etc.

parameters.label: Hour Format
parameters.name: hourformat
parameters.description: ⊞  - 12 hour or 24 hour - Causes the hour channel to cycle through 12 or 24 hours. Also affects the AM/PM channel.

parameters.label: Hour Adjust
parameters.name: houradjust
parameters.description: After the Clock  CHOP  reads the current time, it adds Hour Adjust to pretend the current time is different than the actual current time.

parameters.label: Start  Reference
parameters.name: startref
parameters.description: ⊞  - The date/time that corresponds to year 0, day 1, hour 0, minute 0. It can be relative to Jan 1, 2000 or to the time that the TouchDesigner process started.

parameters.label: Millisecond
parameters.name: msec
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the current millisecond, starting at 0 at the start of a second, going up to 999 at the end of a second. If Output is Fraction, it is the current fraction of a millisecond.

parameters.label: Second
parameters.name: sec
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the current second, starting at 0 for on-the-hour, going up to 59. If Output is Fraction, it is the current fraction of a second (45 seconds past the minute gives .75).

parameters.label: Minute
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the current minute, starting at 0 for on-the-hour, going up to 59. If Output is Fraction, it is the current fraction of a minute (45 seconds past the minute gives .75).

parameters.label: Hour
parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the current hour, starting at 0 for midnight and affected by AM/PM. If Output is Fraction, it is the current fraction of an hour (15 minutes past the hour gives .25), taking into account the current minute and second.

parameters.label: AM/PM
parameters.name: ampm
parameters.description: 0 if before noon, 1 if after noon.

parameters.label: Day of Week
parameters.name: wday
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the actual day of the week, starting with 0 for Monday and 6 for Sunday. If Output is Fraction, it is fraction of a day of the current moment, so at 6:30 PM, it is .77, taking into account the hour, minute and second. To get the fraction for the current time in relation to the week, use the week output.

parameters.label: Day of Month
parameters.name: day
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the actual day of the month, so on March 20, it is 20. If Output is Fraction, this parameter is disabled. To get the fraction for the current time in relation to the month, use the month output.

parameters.label: Day of Year
parameters.name: yday
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the Day of year, starting with 0 for January 1. If it is Fraction, this parameter is disabled. To get the fraction for the current time in relation to the year, use the year output.

parameters.label: Week
parameters.name: week
parameters.description: Week of the year, starting with 0 for the first week and 51 for the last week of the year.

parameters.label: Month
parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Month of the year, starting with 1 for January and 12 for December.

parameters.label: Year
parameters.name: year
parameters.description: If Output is Units, it is the integer year number relative to the Start  Reference , starting at 0, so year 2009 is 9 by default. If Output is Fraction, it is the current fraction of a year, taking into account today's month, day, hour, minute and second.

parameters.label: Latitude
parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enter a latitude (hours/min north/south) of your location. (defaults to Toronto, Canada). Fractional hours are permitted. For example:  43.6532 hours and 0 minutes, is identical to 43 hours and 39 minutes. The parameter latitude1 is hours, latitude2 is minutes.

parameters.label: NS
parameters.name: northsouth
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set if the Latitude value above is in the north or south hemisphere.

parameters.label: Longitude
parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enter a longitude (hours/min east/west) of your location. Fractional hours are permitted. The parameter longitude1 is hours, longitude2 is minutes.

parameters.label: EW
parameters.name: eastwest
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set if the Longitude value above is in the east or west hemisphere.

parameters.label: Moon Phase
parameters.name: moonphase
parameters.description: Outputs the moon phase (0 to 1. .5 is a full moon, 0 and 1 are at the time of the new moon).

parameters.label: Sun Phase
parameters.name: sunphase
parameters.description: (0 to 1, where sunrise=0, sunset = 1, and it reverses down to 0 in time for the sunrise.

parameters.label: Sunrise
parameters.name: sunrise
parameters.description: Outputs the sunrise time (0 to 1, midnight=0, twenty-four hours later = 1).

parameters.label: Sunset
parameters.name: sunset
parameters.description: Outputs the sunset time (0 to 1, midnight=0, twent.y-four hours later = 1).

parameters.label: Declination
parameters.name: declination
parameters.description: (-180 to 180, degrees north/south that the sun is off the equator).

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
